name: Asso Pigliatutto
description: Asso Pigliatutto ('Ace Takes All') is a variant of the classic Italian game Scopa. The defining twist is that playing an Ace allows a player to capture ALL cards on the table instantly. While it simplifies the math for beginners, it adds a layer of 'Ace-hoarding' strategy that changes the flow of the game significantly.

overview.description: Asso Pigliatutto ('Ace Takes All') is a variant of the classic Italian game Scopa. The defining twist is that playing an Ace allows a player to capture ALL cards on the table instantly. While it simplifies the math for beginners, it adds a layer of 'Ace-hoarding' strategy that changes the flow of the game significantly.

history.origins: Developed in Italy as a simplified or faster variation of Scopa. The name explicitly translates to 'Ace Takes All' (Pigliatutto). It is often taught to children as a gateway to standard Scopa because the Ace rule provides exciting, easy captures.
timeline: 1800s: Scopa evolves from earlier fishing games like Primiera.
1900s: Asso Pigliatutto emerges as a popular regional variant, particularly in Southern Italy.
Present: Widely played in Italian cafes and digital apps as 'Scopa d'Assi'.
history.cultural: A staple of Italian social life. 'Scaracoccia' is a regional name used in some dialects.
history.evolution: The introduction of the 'Ace Sweep' mechanic reduced the mental math required for sweeping the table, making the game faster and more aggressive.

setup.deck: 40-card Italian deck (Coins, Cups, Swords, Batons). If using a standard 52-card deck, remove 8s, 9s, and 10s. Kings=10, Queens=9, Jacks=8.
setup.dealing: Dealer gives 3 cards to each player and places 4 cards face-up on the table. When players run out of cards, 3 more are dealt until the deck is empty.

rules.objective: Score 11 points (or 21) by capturing cards, specifically Coins, Sevens, and the 'Primiera'.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Play**: Player plays one card. 2. **Capture**: If the card matches the rank of a table card, it captures it. If it matches the sum of multiple table cards, it captures them. 3. **The Ace Rule**: If you play an Ace, you take ALL cards on the table (unless there is an Ace on the table, in which case you must capture only the Ace). 4. **Scopa**: Clearing the table earns 1 point (a 'Scopa'). Exception: Playing an Ace to clear the table usually does NOT award a Scopa point unless the Ace captured a single Ace. 5. **Refill**: When hands are empty, dealer deals 3 more. 6. **End**: Last player to take a trick collects any remaining table cards.
keyRules: Must Capture: If you can capture, you must. You cannot simply discard if a capture is possible (though you can choose WHICH capture if there are multiple).
Ace Priority: If an Ace is on the table, playing an Ace only captures that Ace (standard capture rule). If NO Ace is on the table, playing an Ace captures EVERYTHING.
Scopa Point: Awarded for clearing the table, marked by turning a card face-up in the trick pile. (Note: Ace-sweeps typically yield 0 points).
Scoring Categories: Settebello (7 of Coins), Denari (Most Coins), Carte (Most Cards), Primiera (Best 4-card set).

strategy.basic: Save Aces for when the table has many cards or high-value cards you can't capture otherwise. Try to leave the table with a sum that the opponent cannot easily capture (e.g., 7 is risky because of Settebello).
strategy.intermediate: Counting Cards: Track whether the Settebello and other 7s have triggered the Primiera point. Don't waste an Ace sweeping 'trash' cards unless you need the card count point.
strategy.advanced: The Ace Trap: If you hold an Ace, you can bait the opponent into filling the table. Conversely, if you know the opponent has an Ace, keep the table lean to minimize their gain.
tips: Never leave a total of 7 on the table if you can avoid it.
In standard Asso Pigliatutto, the Ace sweep is powerful for volume but doesn't give the Scopa point—don't overvalue it for scoring.

synthesis.shortDescription: A simplified, faster variant of Italy's national card game, Scopa. Play an Ace to sweep the board instantly. Capture Coins and Sevens to build your score in this strategic fishing game.
